13	Last Week in Summary.
14	A light week of earnings before we enter preview season the next few weeks, but still a tremendous amount of movement underneath the surface spurred by a big thematic agentic trade.
15	META capped off a 5th week in a row of gains as the Muse hyped continued into and through META Connect and as we await an update on their Watermelon model | On a related note, perceived Muse losers levered to agentic disruption or higher subscription cancellations all finished lower (NYC, OTAs, MTCH, PLNT, Telcos, INTU, CHTR) | The FT reported that GDDY received a takeover offer from GEN, which was met with a lot of investor skepticism | P finished the week up 20% following its investor day which brought a MDD revenue revision and a ~40% EBIT revision on ’28 | 10-year yields continued their move higher making 19-year highs this week | MSFT’s back to trading at ~10-month highs following a Copilot refresh | AKAM with a ~12% intraday fade following a ~$11B compute deal with Anthropic, with lots of pushback on the economics.

105	OAI Developer Day (Tuesday Sept 29th)
106	Registration link here, starts at 1p.
107	The last few days has seen a lot of speculation that OAI will announce an “always-on agent” called “o” during the developer day this week, along with an “ultrafast” API expansion, and likely highlighting GPT-6 Astra which was released earlier in September.
108	On Friday, Fortune also noted that OAI is set to preview a cybersecurity-focused AI model, GPT-6 Cyber, within ​days and launch a new product designed ‌to help customers deploy it more securely and automatically. It will also unveil a new product to help customers deploy the model in a more secure, automated manner.
109	We flagged this last week heading into META Connect given all of the partnership announcements and logos. But recall, this was the price action from the OAI Developer Day last year on October 6th for companies shown or mentioned during the presentation.

136	MDB Investor Day (Wednesday Sept 29th)
137	Registration link here, starts at 11a.
138	Feedback pretty wide ranging overall. Some buy-siders believe this will be more heavily product and strategy focused given it’s CJ’s 1st analyst day. While others think we also get a margin target increase on their 3-5 year framework from 20% to 25%. And then if anything folks think we get a nudge higher on their Atlas growth number from “20%+” to something at most in the L 20’s.
139	Qualitatively, we think folks are looking for details around how their customers are building on AI Apps, maybe better disclosures on Atlas, and then any color on how agents could drive greater consumption.
140	We do think most folks view that Muse was built on Postgress and not a direct beneficiary, but more of what could be the art of the possible down the line. We think there’s a longer lean into the A-Day.

145	Positioning feels mixed at best amongst the HF community, while memory still remains more longed by the LO community relative to other pockets of Semis and the AI ecosystem like Semicaps and large cap compute.
146	Additionally, investor conversations continue to gravitate towards a 100bps q/q step up in GM, and we think there’s a view that we don’t hear much incrementally on the buyback given the CHIPS Act restrictions that rolls off on December 9th. 
147	No pushback on the capex expectation for L $50B’s in FY’27.
148	ACN (Tuesday Sept 29th)
149	6:39a / 8a

151	Conversations / inbounds with LO investors continue to remain almost non-existent, lack of conviction in a NT acceleration in #’s, AI disruption uncertainty, etc. On the HF side, while a lot of the relative alpha for ACN intra Q felt almost entirely tied to the unwind, SI still remains fairly elevated relative to historicals.
152	And if there are any longs into the print, it feels more driven from the fact that Fed checks have been good, some security exposure, and the stocks still trading at LDD P/E.

157	Blayne’s Semi Takes.
158	Blayne and team recap a busy week of read throughs in Semis, noting that each Muse user is allocated 2 vCPUs powered by an 88-core AMD EPYC 9D64 (Genoa) processor or 126-core EPYC 9D25. The configuration is a positive readthrough for CPUs, but the lack of visibility on concurrency makes it difficult to forecast the magnitude of incremental demand but his assumptions indicate 10s of thousands not 100s of incremental CPU demand. 
159	Additionally, he updated his optical model as 1.6T ramps faster than expected, with AI transceiver demand approaching 180M units in C27 and 245M in C28. NPO design activity is accelerating, while meaningful scale-up CPO adoption looks further out.

169	Thought this was an interesting chart on AI rack BOM mix by platform. Sherman and team note “Networking rises from 8.6% in GB300 to 18.5% in Taycann and 22.4% in NVL576 as inter-rack optical and external scale-out fabric expand.”
